data.name: Arunava
data.gender_notes: Arunava is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arunava is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Aruna’, which means 'dawn' or 'red'. In Hindu mythology, Arunava is the name of the god of dawn and the charioteer of the sun god Surya. The name is believed to symbolize the beginning of a new day and the promise of a fresh start. The name Arunava carries the meaning “God of Dawn” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arunava usually hope their child will grow to embody god of dawn and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the dawn of new beginnings and the promise of a fresh start.
data.etymology: Arunava belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Dawn.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arunava total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

The name Arunava, representing such a powerful deity, imparts these virtues to the one who is given this name. historical_references.reference: Arunava was a famous Jaina monk and philosopher from Karnataka, India. He lived during the 12th and 13th centuries and is considered one of the greatest scholars of the Jaina tradition. He wrote commentaries on various Jaina texts and is best known for his work on the 'Tattvartha Sutra'.

Arunavasimha was a prominent poet and scholar in medieval Bengal, India. He lived during the 10th century and is known for his works in Sanskrit and Bengali languages, including the 'Arunakhanda' and 'Arunavabhasha'. He was a court poet for the Pala king Mahipal and is considered one of the greatest figures in Bengali literature.
